body.p: Witch (a tale).[ShA:] For the beginning of the tale there is a significantly different variant in the TeNM's archive data of this text, at the same presumably related to the same recording process. The Enets text prensented here has two slightly There lived a witch together with a true human woman. The witch had one daughter, the woman had two daughters.different versions, and for the beginning even three versions. At first, they lived well with one another, but then their relationship went bad. One day the witch said to her fellow. Woman, woman, let's go for hay. The woman said. I'll sew up the holes in the children's boot, and then we'll go. The witch went home. The woman said to her daughters. My little ones, it seems the giant will eat me up, run away from the tent. When you go, follow straight the direction of the sun. Your old grandparents live at the sunset.[ShA:] KazaxuuriÊ and dÊ¼isixuuriÊ are You will reach the shore of a large lake. Cry from this shore.morphologicall unexpected forms, kazaxuuziÊ and dÊ¼isixuuziÊ are expected instead.Grandfather, grandmother, take us to you! Your grandfather will come out of the water. The woman said these words before she left. Then the woman and the witch went for hay. They went for long or not, but they found hay. They began to collect hay. At some point the witch said. Woman, woman, have you seen any lice on me? They sat down in the sun. First, the woman began to look for lice of the witch. The witch's lice are leeches. The woman is very afraid of them.[ShA:] Normally the lexical item is translates as beetle, but here I follow the translation of this text. The woman does not eat the witch's lice, but throws them away like nits. Having seen this, the witch said. Why are you throwing my lice, why don't you eat them? The woman got completely afraid. Then the witch said. Woman, woman, let me also look for your lice. The witch began to look for the woman's lice. She said to the woman. Oh, oh, your lice smell. And she throws the women's lice no matter where. And at some point, when the woman was lying like that, she pierced one of her ears with an awl. The woman died. Having wrapped the woman's corpse in the grass, she took it home. She hid it there. The woman's children still saw their mother in the hay when the witch was carrying her. The elder one said to her sister. The witch killed our mother, let's run away. The witch came to their tent and said. Your mother will come soon. You go to sleep. Don't go anywhere. After that she went home. The girls caught baby birds near the tent and put them in tent covers. After that they ran away. They took with them their mother's comb, thimble, hand ring, and mallet. The girls ran away towards the sunset. The witch is always listening. In the woman's tent, baby birds play all the time. The witch said to her daughter. Wait, Iâll cook the food for you later, Iâll eat my food. Having finished eating, the witch went to the woman's tent to kill the children. As she looked to the tent covers, baby birds flew out. The witch became very angry. She thought to herself. Oh these devils, they have cheated me, Iâd better go after them. So she began to pursue them. The girls look, the witch is already catching them up. The elder one threw her mother's comb over her head. A large forest appeared behind them. While the witch was passing through this forest, the girls ran far away. Then the witch began to catch them up again. The older girl threw her mother's thimble over her head. He became a big hill. While the witch walked around this hill, the girls again ran far away. The witch is catching them up again. The elder girl threw her mother's hand ring. It became a huge lake. While the witch walked around this lake, the girls again ran far away. The witch began to catch them up again. The eldest threw her mother's mallet. It became a huge bank. While the witch was climbing at this bank, she broke all her nails. The girls went down to the bank of a large river. They started crying. Grandfather, grandmother, take us to you! There is a large tent on the other side of the river. A completely black old woman came out of this tent. She said. What am I like? The elder girl said. You are very nice. Then the old woman whistled. A big nelma appeared from under the water. She put the girls on her back and transported them to the old womanâs tent. At some point, the witch came down to the river bank. She cried. Give me a boat! The old woman went outside and said. What am I like? You look like the devil, your face is terrible, said the witch. The old woman whistled. A big taimen appeared from under the water near the witch. The witch sat on its back. In the middle of the river, the taimen [ShA:] My interpretation of Ð±Ð°ÑÐ¸Ð¼Ð° is unsure.overturned and the witch drowned. The girls lived with their grandmother for a long time. They have even become adult women. One day their grandmother said. Why don't you look for a good life. She gave them a copper boat. The girls left. They went for a long time or not, but the younger girl died. The elder one put the corpse of her sister in a bearâs lay and said. Grandfather, take care of her! Then she left. She went for a long time or not, but stopped and landed. There is a rotten tree on the ground. The girl said. Let me rest here. She sat down near the rotten tree. And the witch came out from there and said. Let's go together. So they went by foot. They walked for long or not, but they saw. Two men are riding towards them. One of the riders has everything black, and the other one has everything white. The witch said. I will take the one who is has everything white as my husband. They both sat down on the people's sledges. The witch sat on the sledge of the one who had everything white. They reached home. People got very glad. Of course. The young men took wives for themselves. They started living. One day old men said. Let's light a big fire outdoors and test our daughters-in-law to see if they know how to cook meat. The witch said. I'll be the first to cook. As soon as the witch reached the fire, people pushed her into the fire. Before her death, the witch cried. My leeches, go all over the earth! Her leeches became mosquitoes. This is the end.
